_comment: SIZE AXIS on the varying-rule rung: does the in-context-learning threshold
move with parameter count?
This is the experiment the ladder position in research/findings.md is least
able to generalize from. Every other result here is a statement about ONE
cell -- 492,418 params -- and 'the model does not do ICL' means nothing about
whether that is a property of the architecture or of the scale. This sweeps
d_model on the rung where ICL is actually tested, so a threshold that moves
with size is directly observable.
The sweep tool sets d_model, derives n_heads = d_model/64, and holds
head_dim at 64, so the change is width rather than head layout. Sizes:
d_model 128 -> 492,418 params (the cell every other result used)
d_model 192 -> ~1.1M
d_model 256 -> ~1.8M
d_model 384 -> ~3.2M
Read with off_pair_rate, not byte accuracy alone. On a 3-symbol alphabet
chance is 0.333, so a weak competence is hard to see; off_pair (emitting a
symbol that is neither the query's nor the target's) is the readout that a
positional bias cannot game.
ON CONFOUNDS: an earlier version of this comment claimed steps are held at
600 across sizes so larger models are less-trained per parameter. That is
wrong, and worth stating because the auto-batch tuner is exactly what makes
it wrong: the tuner holds the EFFECTIVE batch (batch x accum) fixed, so
samples-per-optimizer-step -- and therefore epochs over the ~360-instance
training pool -- are constant across model sizes. Memory pressure cannot
leak into the optimization here.
The confound that IS live is gradient noise at a fixed effective batch:
holding it constant is what makes the axis comparable, but it also means
every size here sees the same batch, so a size that would prefer a larger
one is handicapped rather than helped. That argues for the opposite of the
usual confound and is the first thing to revisit if the axis comes back
flat.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/size-axis-varying-rule.json params gpu 128 192 256 384 --seeds=0,1,2
